verses.zh: 以色列人哪，你们当听耶和华的话。耶和华与这地的居民争辩，因这地上无诚实，无良善，无人认识　神。
verses.en: Listen to the Lord’s message, you Israelites![NOTE:1] For the Lord has a covenant lawsuit[NOTE:2] against the people of Israel.[NOTE:3] For there is neither faithfulness nor loyalty in the land, nor do they acknowledge God.[NOTE:4]
notes: Heb “sons of Israel” (so NASB); cf. KJV “children of Israel,” and NAB, NRSV “people of Israel.”

The noun רִיב (riv, “dispute, lawsuit”) is used in two contexts: (1) nonlegal contexts: (a) “dispute” between individuals (e.g., Gen 13:7; Isa 58:1; Jer 15:10) or (b) “brawl; quarrel” between people (e.g., Exod 17:7; Deut 25:1); and (2) legal contexts: (a) “lawsuit; legal process” (e.g., Exod 23:3-6; Deut 19:17; 21:5; Ezek 44:24; Ps 35:23), (b) “lawsuit; legal case” (e.g., Deut 1:12; 17:8; Prov 18:17; 25:9), and (c) God’s “lawsuit” on behalf of a person or against his own people (Hos 4:1; 12:3; Mic 6:2; HALOT 1225-26 s.v. רִיב). The term in Hosea refers to a covenant lawsuit in which Yahweh the suzerain lodges a legal case against his disobedient vassal, accusing Israel and Judah of breach of covenant that will elicit the covenant curses.
Heb “with the inhabitants of the land” (so KJV); cf. NAB, NASB, NRSV “against the inhabitants of the land.”
Heb “there is no truthfulness nor loyalty nor knowledge of God in the land.” Here “knowledge of God” refers to recognition of his authority and obedience to his will.
verses.commentary:
4:1

NASB
"Listen to the word of the

Lord"

NKJV, NRSV, REB, JPSOA, Peshitta
"Hear the word of the Lord"

TEV
"Listen to what he says"

NJB
"Hear what Yahweh says"

The VERB (BDB 1033, KB 1570, Qal IMPERATIVE) means to
hear so as to perform. It is used several times in Hosea (cf. Hosea 4:1; 5:1; 9:17), but many times in the other eighth
century prophets.

- Amos, 3:1,13; 4:1; 5:1; 7:16; 8:4,11

- Micah, 1:2; 3:1,9; 5:15; 6:1[twice],2,9; 7:7

See note at Amos 3:1.

SPECIAL TOPIC: LISTEN/HEAR (shema)

▣ "the Lord has a case" This term (BDB 936) has two main senses.

- a legal lawsuit, Isa. 1:23; 3:13-26; 41:21; Jer. 2:9-13; 25:31; 50:34; Hosea 4:1; 12:3; Micah 6:1-5; 7:9-13

- a dispute or controversy, Isa. 41:11; 58:4; Jer. 15:10; Hosea 2:2

YHWH is victim, prosecuting attorney, and judge (see G. B. Caird, The Language and Imagery of the
Bible, p. 157)! The court case is one of three common literary
techniques used by the prophets.

- legal case (i.e. divorce case)

- funeral dirge (judgment oracle)

- salvation promise (deliverance oracle)

▣ "against the inhabitants of the land" The land of Palestine/Canaan had a special theological
significance. This starts with God's promise to Abraham to give him a seed, a name, and a land (cf. Gen. 12:1-1). This
promise is reaffirmed in a special "covenant trance" in Gen. 15:12-21. The land will be cleansed of Canaanite
fertility worship (cf. Hosea 4:16). When the people of God become involved in the same abominations they, too,
must be cleansed from YHWH's land!

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT PROMISES TO THE PATRIARCHS

SPECIAL TOPIC: CONSEQUENCES OF IDOLATRY

▣

NASB, NRSV, TEV
"faithfulness"

NKJV
"truth"

NJB

JPSOA

REB
"good faith"

LXX

Peshitta

The NOUN "faithful" (BDB 54) is negated. This is a major theological term. It
clearly states mankind's part of the covenant with YHWH. In the opening verse of chapter 4, several major theological
issues are highlighted.

- faithfulness, v. 1

- loyalty (i.e. lovingkindness), v. 1

- knowledge

Doing a personal study on these NOUNS would be a great help to your personal Bible
study. All believers should check for themselves what others say the Bible "says. . ." We are responsible for our own theology!

For another Hebrew root (BDB 325 II), which denotes this same faithfulness, see the note at Hosea 10:2.

SPECIAL TOPIC: BELIEVE, TRUST, FAITH and FAITHFULNESS IN THE OT

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT

▣

NASB
"kindness"

NKJV, LXX, Peshitta
"mercy"

NRSV, REB
"loyalty"

TEV
"love"

NJB
"faith"

JPSOA
"goodness"

This is the Hebrew word hesed (BDB 338, cf. Hosea 6:4; 10:12; 12:6). This is a
very important theological concept. Be sure to see the Special Topic below.

SPECIAL TOPIC: LOVINGKINDNESS (hesed)

▣ "no. . .knowledge of God" This is the theme (e.g. Hosea 2:20; 4:6; 5:4; 6:6,6) of the book—that we
should know God, not as an object (an "it," an idol), but in a personal, intimate relationship (a person).

The term "know"
(BDB 395) in the OT is related to a personal, intimate relationship (cf. Gen. 2:20; 4:1; Jer. 1:5). The marvelous
part of this truth is that not only can sinful humans know God, but that they are known by Him (cf. Jer. 31:34;
Heb. 8:1ff). He seeks us!

SPECIAL TOPIC: KNOW

SPECIAL TOPIC: Seek the Lord

verses.zh: 但起假誓，不践前言，杀害，偷盗，奸淫，行强暴，杀人流血，接连不断。
verses.en: There is only cursing, lying, murder, stealing, and adultery.They resort to violence and bloodshed.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “they break out, and bloodshed touches bloodshed.” The Hebrew term פָּרַץ (parats, “to break out”) refers to violent and wicked actions (BDB 829 s.v. פָּרַץ 7; HALOT 972 s.v. פרץ 6.c). It is used elsewhere in a concrete sense to describe breaking through physical barriers. Here it is used figuratively to describe breaking moral barriers and restraints (cf. TEV “Crimes increase, and there is one murder after another”).
verses.commentary:
4:2 Instead of faithfulness, kindness, and knowledge, Israel was depicted by the terms mentioned in
Hosea 4:2 (all INFINITIVE ABSOLUTES), which refer to the breaking of the Ten Commandments
(i.e. specifically the 2nd, 6th, 7th, and 8th). The Ten Commandments are God's will for mankind in society. They
are not given to restrict mankind's freedom, but to accentuate his communal happiness! But Israel knowingly
broke all moral boundaries (BDB 829, KB 971, Qal PERFECT)!

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE TEN COMMANDMENTS

▣ "swearing, deception" It is possible that those two sins also reflect the Ten Commandments (but different terms).

- swearing = Exod. 20:7; Deut. 5:11

- deception = Exod. 20:16; Deut. 5:20

See Gordon Fee, Douglas Stuart, How To Read the Bible For All Its Worth, pp. 187-188.

▣ "murder" See SPECIAL TOPIC: MURDER.

▣ " "stealing" See SPECIAL TOPIC: STEAL.

▣ "adultery" See SPECIAL TOPIC: ADULTERY.

verses.zh: 因此，这地悲哀，其上的民、田野的兽、空中的鸟必都衰微，海中的鱼也必消灭。
verses.en: Therefore the land will mourn, and all its inhabitants will perish.[NOTE:1] The wild animals,[NOTE:2] the birds of the sky, and even the fish in the sea will perish.
notes: Or “languish” (so KJV, NRSV); cf. NIV “waste away.”
Heb “the beasts of the field” (so NAB, NIV).
verses.commentary:
4:3 "everyone who lives in it languishes" The term (BDB 51, KB 63, Pulal PERFECT with waw )
means to become weak and by connotation weak by drought (e.g. Joel 1:10; Isa. 16:8; 24:4; 33:9; Jer. 12:4). The fire
(i.e. drought) of YHWH's Deuteronomic judgments (cf. Leviticus 26 and Deuteronomy 28) has come (cf. Amos 7:4).

- the land mourns

- the people languish

- the animals disappear

Physical creation (especially YHWH's Promised Land) was affected by mankind's sin (cf. Gen. 3:17-19;
Rom. 8:18-25). This passage is a divine judgment even more severe than the flood (cf. Gen. 6-9) because even the fish
are affected (cf. Zeph. 1:2-3). Ironically judgment from too much water (Genesis 6) is now judgment from not enough water
(i.e. drought)! Chaos has returned!

SPECIAL TOPIC: WATERS/SEA

verses.zh: 然而，人都不必争辩，也不必指责，因为这民与抗拒祭司的人一样。
verses.en: Do not let anyone accuse or contend against anyone else,[NOTE:1] for my case is against you priests![NOTE:2]
notes: Or “Let no one contend or accuse.”

The singular noun כֹּהֵן (cohen, “priest”) may be understood as a singular of number (so KJV, NASB, NRSV), referring to a singular individual (perhaps the high priest); however, it is more likely that it functions as a collective singular, referring to the priesthood as a whole (e.g., 4:7-10, so NAB, NCV, TEV, NLT, CEV). Collective singular forms alternate with plural forms throughout the oracle against the priests in 4:4-10.tc The MT reads וְעַמְּךָ כִּמְרִיבֵי כֹהֵן (veʿammekha kimrive khohen), “And your people [are] like those who contend against the priest.” This is reflected in the LXX and the versions; however, it is syntactically awkward and makes little sense in context. Several textual critics suggest emending the text to read וְעִמְּךָ רִיבִי כֹהֵן (veʿimmekha rivi khohen), “My contention is with/against you, O priest!” This involves (1) the revocalization of עַמְּךָ (“your people”) to עִמְּךָ (“with/against you”) and (2) positing dittography (a letter written twice instead of once) of כְּ (kaf) between original וְעַמְּךָ רִיבִי to create וְעַמְּךָ כִּרִיבִי (MT). The BHS editors suggest that the MT should be emended. However, the editors of the Hebrew Old Testament Text Project retain the MT reading with a “B” rating. Likewise, the English translations are split: (1) KJV “for thy people are as they that strive with the priest”; NASB “for your people are like those who contend with the priest”; and NIV “for your people are like those who bring charges against a priest”; and (2) RSV “for with you is my contention, O priest”; NJPS: “for this your people has a grievance against [you], O priest!”; TEV “my complaint is against you priests”; and CEV “My case is against you, the priests!”
verses.commentary:
4:4 The first two VERBS are JUSSIVES:

- let no one find fault, Qal JUSSIVE (BDB 936, KB 1224)

- let none offer reproof, Hiphil JUSSIVE (BDB 406, KB 410)

These both have legal connotations (e.g. #1 Jdg. 6:31-32; #2 Amos 5:10). But who is the speaker in 4a?

- an unnamed objector (cf. Amos 5:10)

- a priestly representative (i.e. High Priest)

- the nation of Israel (represented by a priest and prophet)

- YHWH Himself (the Judge speaks, cf. Hosea 4:5c)

▣

NASB, NKJV
"For you people are like those who contend

with the priest"

NRSV, NET
"For with you is my contention, O priest"

TEV. REB
"my complaint is against you priests"

NJB
"it is you, priest, that I denounce"

JPSOA
"for this your people has a grievance against

you], O priest"

Peshitta
"for your people is engaged in controversy like

a priest"

LXX
"but my people are as a priest spoken against"

The NASB does not fit the context well. A different revocalization and a doubling of one
consonant can result in "My contention is against you, O Priests" (RSV; see good note in NET Bible, p. 1562, #15),
which fits the context (cf. Hosea 4:6) better.

The UBS Text Project, p. 231, supports the MT (NASB) reading with a "B" rating (some doubt) with the
suggested translation:

"and your people (are) like (people) contending against the priest"

verses.zh: 你这祭司必日间跌倒；先知也必夜间与你一同跌倒；我必灭绝你的母亲。
verses.en: You stumble day and night, and the false prophets stumble with you;you have destroyed your own people.[NOTE:1]
notes: Or “and I will destroy your mother” (so NASB, NRSV).tc The MT reads וְדָמִיתִי אִמֶּךָ (vedamiti ’immekha, “and I will destroy your mother”), and is followed by most English versions; however, the text should probably be emended to וְדָמִית עַמֶּךָ (vedamit ’ammekha, “and you have destroyed your own people”). The second person masculine singular form וְדָמִית (vedamit, “and you have destroyed”) is preserved in several medieval Hebrew mss and reflected in Jerome’s Vulgate. For discussion in favor of the MT reading, see D. Barthélemy, ed., Preliminary and Interim Report on the Hebrew Old Testament Text Project, 5:232.
verses.commentary:
4:5 The VERB "stumble" (BDB 505, KB 502, Qal PERFECT with
waw) is repeated twice. To stumble is the opposite imagery of "faithfulness" (i.e. sure footedness).

▣

NASB, NKJV, NRSV
"And I will destroy your mother"

TEV
"and I am going to destroy Israel, your

mother"

NJB
"and I will make your mother perish"

JPSOA
"And I will destroy your kindred"

REB
"your nation is brought to ruin"

LXX
"I have made your mother like night"

Peshitta
"and yet your mother keeps silent"

The NET Bible (p. 1562) suggests an emendation (two consonant changes). "You have
destroyed your own people." This then would not be a quote from YHWH, but the first in a series of condemnations
of the priests. Priests are condemned

- for not teaching the truth of YHWH's covenant

- for living lives of corrupted fertility practices

The UBS Text Project, p. 232, gives the MT a "B" rating, which means YHWH is the actor bringing
judgment on the Northern Kingdom. The specific judgment is "silence" (KB 225 II).

- no teaching

- no worship

- no songs

- silent like the dead

verses.zh: 我的民因无知识而灭亡。你弃掉知识，我也必弃掉你，使你不再给我作祭司。你既忘了你　神的律法，我也必忘记你的儿女。
verses.en: You have destroyed[NOTE:1] my people by failing to acknowledge me! Because you refuse to acknowledge me,[NOTE:2] I will reject you as my priests.Because you reject[NOTE:3] the law of your God,I will reject[NOTE:4] your descendants.
notes: Heb “they have destroyed” or “my people are destroyed” (so KJV, NIV, NRSV).
Heb “Because you reject knowledge”; cf. NLT “because they don’t know me.”
Heb “have forgotten”; cf. NAB, NIV “have ignored.”
Heb “forget” (so KJV, NRSV); cf. NLT “forget to bless.”
verses.commentary:
4:6 "My people are destroyed for lack of knowledge.

Because you have rejected knowledge" The term "destroy"
(BDB 198, KB 225, Niphal PERFECT) means "to cut off" and thereby to cease to exist. The
people were guilty, not because they did not understand, but because they knowingly turned away and rejected
(BDB 549, KB 540, Qal PERFECT) YHWH's covenant. This was especially true of the religious and political leaders.

SPECIAL TOPIC: KEEP

▣ "I also will reject you from being My priest" The nation of Israel was meant to be priests to all the world
(cf. Exod. 19:4-6; see SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN).
Here, however, it refers to the local Levites who were to instruct the people in the law of God (cf. Lev. 10:11;
Deut. 17:10-11; 33:10; Jer. 18:18; Mal. 2:6-7), which they did not!

▣ "Since you have forgotten the law of your God" Knowledge has two aspects:

- personal relationship

- covenant obligations

They forgot (BDB 1013, KB 1489, Qal IMPERFECT with waw) YHWH and
His covenant so He will forget (Qal IMPERFECT) their descendants. This is a reversal of the
covenant promises of Exod. 20:6 and Deut. 5:10; 7:9! Priests (and Levites) were to be the teachers of Israel, but they
became the corruptors of Israel! They could no longer serve as sacrificial offerers!

verses.zh: 祭司越发增多，就越发得罪我；我必使他们的荣耀变为羞辱。
verses.en: The more the priests increased in numbers, the more they rebelled against me.They have turned[NOTE:1] their glorious calling into a shameful disgrace!
notes: The MT reads אָמִיר (ʾamir, “I will change, exchange”; Hiphil imperfect first person common singular from מוּר, mur, “to change, exchange”). However, an alternate scribal tradition (tiqquneh sopherim, that is, an intentional scribal change when the Masoretes believed that the received consonantal reading was defective) preserves the reading הֵמִירוּ (hemiru, “they have exchanged”; Hiphil perfect third person common plural from מוּר). This alternate scribal tradition is also found in the Targum and reflected in the Syriac Peshitta. Several translations follow the MT; KJV, RSV, and NASB have, “I will change their glory into shame,” and the TEV has, “I will turn your honor into disgrace.” However, others adopt the alternate tradition; the NRSV has, “they changed their glory into shame,” and the NIV84, “they exchanged their Glory for something disgraceful”; NIV11, “they exchanged their glorious God for something disgraceful.” For discussion in favor of the MT reading, see D. Barthélemy, ed., Preliminary and Interim Report on the Hebrew Old Testament Text Project, 5:232.
verses.commentary:
4:7 "The more they multiplied, the more they sinned against Me" "They" seems to refer to the people who were
bringing sacrifices to the priests who performed cultic activities (cf. Hosea 4:8-10). The more God gave His people, the
more they turned away from Him (see a similar example using the prophets in Hosea 11:2).

▣

NASB, NKJV, LXX
"I will change their glory into shame"

NRSV, Peshitta
"they changed their glory into shame"

TEV
"I will turn your honor into disgrace"

NJB
"they have bartered their Glory for Shame"

JPSOA
"I will change their dignity to dishonor"

REB
"their dignity I shall turn into dishonor"

NET
"They have turned their glorious calling

into a shameful disgrace"

As you can see from the translations the textual issue is over who the subject is, YHWH
(NASB, TEV) or Israel (NRSV, NJB). The MT has YHWH as the subject (BDB 558, KB 560, Hiphil
IMPERFECT). However, Jewish tradition changes the VERB to a Hiphil
PERFECT. This emendation is followed by the Jewish Targums (Aramaic translation and
commentaries) and the Peshitta (Syrian Christian translation).

The UBS Text Project, p. 232, gives "I will change their glory" a "B" rating.

The term "shame" (BDB 885) is the opposite of "honor" (cf. Ps. 83:16; Prov. 3:35; 13:18). In
this context it refers to idolatry (cf. Hosea 4:18). They shared YHWH's glory as His covenant people, but they
exchanged this for self-centered sexual fertility worship (the glory of Ba'al).

SPECIAL TOPIC: SHAME

SPECIAL TOPIC: GLORY (kabod, OT)

verses.zh: 他们吃我民的赎罪祭，满心愿意我民犯罪。
verses.en: They feed on the sin offerings of my people;their appetites long for their iniquity!
verses.commentary:
4:8 "They feed on the sin of My people,

And direct their desire toward their iniquity" This seems
to relate to the priests' lusting after their portion of the meat of the sin offerings (cf. Lev. 6 : 26), but metaphorically it
implies that they joined in the fertility rites.

The phrase "direct their desire toward" is literally "lift one's soul to." It is used six times in
this sense (cf. Deut. 24:15; Ps. 24:4; Prov. 19:18; Jer. 22:27; 44:14, and here).

verses.zh: 将来民如何，祭司也必如何；我必因他们所行的惩罚他们，照他们所做的报应他们。
verses.en: I will deal with the people and priests together:[NOTE:1] I will punish them both for their ways, and I will repay them for their deeds.
notes: Heb “And it shall be, like people, like priest” (so ASV); cf. NAB “The priests shall fare no better than the people.”
verses.commentary:
4:9 "like people, like priest" This is a common proverb which reflects an obvious truth as the priests
were to be judged for their known sin, so too, the people.

▣ "I will punish them for their ways" The VERB (BDB 823, KB 955, Qal
PERFECT with waw) basically means "to visit" or "attend to." YHWH can visit for blessing
or judgment, based on the covenant fidelity of the people (cf. Leviticus 26; Deuteronomy 28).

verses.zh: 他们吃，却不得饱；行淫，而不得立后；因为他们离弃耶和华，不遵他的命。
verses.en: They will eat, but not be satisfied;they will engage in prostitution, but not increase in numbersbecause they have abandoned the Lordby pursuing other gods.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “by guarding harlotry.” The present translation assumes that the first word of v. 11 in the Hebrew text is to be taken with the infinitive at the end of v. 10 (so also NAB, NIV, NCV, NRSV).
verses.commentary:
4:10 Though they seek fertility idols, they will not find enough food, nor children (e.g. Hag. 1:6)! The growth
in population implied in Hosea 4:7a is now at an end!

There are interesting articles in

- the IVP Bible Background Commentary (OT), p. 754

- NIDOTTE, vol. 1, pp. 1122-1125

which mention several types of prostitutes in the ANE.

- commercial prostitution

- temple prostitution

verses.zh: 奸淫和酒，并新酒，夺去人的心。
verses.en: Old and new wine take away the understanding of my people.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “take away the heart of my people.” The present translation assumes that the first word of v. 12 in the Hebrew text is to be construed with the noun at the end of v. 11 (so also TEV, CEV, NLT).
verses.commentary:
4:11 This is obviously a proverb. Sin robs people of moral sight and they grope in darkness as drunk,
blind men" (cf. Isa. 28:1-4). This may specifically refer to Canaanite festivals at certain times of the ripening grape harvests.

SPECIAL TOPIC: BIBLICAL ATTITUDES TOWARD ALCOHOL AND ALCOHOL ABUSE

verses.zh: 我的民求问木偶，以为木杖能指示他们；因为他们的淫心使他们失迷，他们就行淫离弃　神，不守约束，
verses.en: They consult their wooden idols, and their diviner’s staff answers with an oracle.The wind of prostitution blows them astray;they commit spiritual adultery[NOTE:1] against their God.
notes: Heb “adultery.” The adjective “spiritual” is supplied in the translation to clarify that apostasy is meant here.
verses.commentary:
4:12 Israel was seeking to know the future and control it by improper means (cf. Deut. 18:9-13).

SPECIAL TOPIC: MAGIC

▣

NASB
"wooden idol"

NKJV
"wooden idols"

NRSV, TEV, REB
"a piece of wood"

NJB
"a block of wood"

JPSOA
"stick"

LXX
"rods"

Peshitta
"staff"

This term (BDB 781) means "tree" or "wood." A slightly different form is used in Hosea 4:17; 8:4;
13:2; 14:8 and means "idols." Since this is paralleled with rod/wand/staff it may refer to a tree oracle (i.e. Ezek. 21:21) or a reference
to the Asherah pole/carved stake (i.e. Exod. 34:13-16) and not a humanoid-shaped wooden idol. The JPSOA footnote suggests it refers
to a phallus symbol (i.e. Ba'al, the male fertility god of Canaan).

▣

NASB, REB
"diviner's wand"

NKJV, Peshitta
"staff"

NRSV
"divining rod"

TEV, NJB
"stick"

JPSOA
"rod"

This term (BDB 596) means "a tree," "a staff," or "a rod." Some of its uses are:

- a wooden weapon (cf. 1 Sam. 17:40,43; Ezek. 29:9)

- a walking stick (cf. Gen. 32:20; Exod. 12:11)

- a stick to control an animal (cf. Num. 22:27)

- young trees (e.g. Gen. 30:37-39, 41; Jer. 1:1)

- a shepherd's staff (cf. Zech. 11:7,10,14, see NIDOTTE, vol. 2, p. 1088)

SPECIAL TOPIC: DIVINATION

▣ "a spirit of harlotry" The term "spirit" has nothing to do with demon possession here, but it
is used in the OT for "mindset," "character" or "energizing center." Here is a list of how this term is used to
express human characteristics or feelings:

- bitterness of spirit, Gen. 26:35

- shortness of spirit, Exod. 6:9

- oppressed in spirit, 1 Sam. 1:15

- sullen in spirit, 1 Kgs. 21:5

- impatient in spirit, Job 21:4; Prov. 14:29

- haughty in spirit vs. humble in spirit, Prov. 16:18-19; Isa. 66:2

- faithful of spirit, Prov. 11:13

- staggering in spirit, Isa. 19:14

- grieved in spirit, Isa. 54:6

This describes Israel's lust after the fertility gods of Canaan (cf. Hosea 5:4). The interpretive issues
were these cultic sexual acts (cf. Hosea 4:3-14) or it could be imagery of unfaithfulness (e.g. Exod. 34:15-16;
Lev. 20:5; Jdg. 2:17; 8:27,33; 1 Chr. 5:25; Ps. 73:27; 106:39).

SPECIAL TOPIC: SPIRIT IN THE BIBLE

▣ "departing from their God" Literally this is "from under God" (BDB 1065), implying their
deserting YHWH's authority.

verses.zh: 在各山顶，各高冈的橡树、杨树、栗树之下，献祭烧香，因为树影美好。所以，你们的女儿淫乱，你们的新妇（或译：儿妇；下同）行淫。
verses.en: They sacrifice on the mountaintops and burn offerings on the hills;they sacrifice[NOTE:1] under oak, poplar, and terebinth,because their shade is so pleasant.As a result, your daughters have become cult prostitutes,and your daughters-in-law commit adultery!
notes: The phrase “they sacrifice” is not repeated in the Hebrew text here but is implied by parallelism; it is provided in the translation for the sake of clarity.
verses.commentary:
4:13 "They offer sacrifices. . .burn incense" These could refer to two separate cultic acts or just incense
burning. No sacrificial altars are connected to local Ba'al worship.

▣ "on the top of the mountains. . .on the hills" This could refer to two things:

- the highest part of the topography was the site of the local Ba'al altar

- the altars of Ba'al/Astarte were made of cut stones with a central phallic symbol (raised pillar) and an
Asherah carved pole or live tree (cf. Deut. 12:2; Jer. 2:20; 3:6; Ezek. 6:13)

▣ "oak, poplar, and terebinth" Trees marked sacred sites because they reflected the presence
of underground water, which was extremely important for desert people. There is no record of Israel ever
worshiping trees, although they held them to be sacred sites (e.g. Gen. 13:18; Jdg. 4:5). In this context the
trees were used as shade for the fertility practices of Ba'al (cf. Deut. 12:2; Jer. 2:20; 3:6; 13:27; 17:2; Hosea 4:13).

SPECIAL TOPIC: TREES

verses.zh: 你们的女儿淫乱，你们的新妇行淫，我却不惩罚她们；因为你们自己离群与娼妓同居，与妓女一同献祭。这无知的民必致倾倒。
verses.en: I will not punish your daughters when they commit prostitution,nor your daughters-in-law when they commit adultery.For the men consort with harlots; they sacrifice with temple prostitutes.It is true:[NOTE:1] “A people that lacks understanding will come to ruin!”
notes: The words “it is true” are supplied in the translation to indicate that this is a conclusion drawn on the preceding behavior (cf. NAB “So must a people”; NRSV “thus a people”; TEV “As the proverb says, ‘A people’”).
verses.commentary:
4:14 It is possible that these statements are really questions expecting a "yes" answer. There is no double
standard with God. Both men and women are condemned for their promiscuous fertility rites (cf. Deut. 23:17-18). There
are three types of women involved:

- new brides

- cultic prostitutes

- other local women

It is also grammatically and contextually possible to see the priests as the recipients of the cultic
acts of Hosea 4:14. The priests who should have known better, also participated in the sexual activities and set a
disastrous pattern for the community! If this is accurate, then the women mentioned in Hosea 4:13 may be the priests' own families!

verses.zh: 以色列啊，你虽然行淫，犹大却不可犯罪。不要往吉甲去，不要上到伯・亚文，也不要指着永生的耶和华起誓。
verses.en: Although you, O Israel, commit adultery,do not let Judah become guilty!Do not journey to Gilgal. Do not go up to Beth Aven.[NOTE:1] Do not swear, “As surely as the Lord lives!”
notes: Beth Aven means “house of wickedness” in Hebrew; it is a polemic reference to “Bethel,” which means “house of God” (cf. CEV “at sinful Bethel”).
verses.commentary:
4:15 This verse has a series of JUSSIVES:

- "Do not let Judah become guilty" (BDB 79, KB 95, Qal JUSSIVE)

- "Do not go to Gilgad" (BDB 97, KB 112, Qal JUSSIVE)

- "Do not go up to Beth-aven" (BDB 748, KB 828, Qal JUSSIVE)

- "Take the oath" (BDB 989, KB 1396, Niphal JUSSIVE)

It seems Hosea was written to both Israel and Judah.

▣ "Though you, Israel, play the harlot, Do not let Judah become guilty" This plea is paralleled in Ezekiel 23
(cf. Jer. 3:6-18). Judah should have seen and feared, but she did not! She is even more responsible!

▣ "Do not go to Gilgal" This was a possible reference to the site of the first campsite of Joshua
when the Israelites entered the Promised Land (cf. Josh. 4:20). It had now become an idolatrous shrine (see notes at Amos 4:4; 5:5).
The other possibility is that it refers to a northern Gilgal, which was the location of a school of the prophets
(cf. 2 Kgs. 2:1; 4:38), which later became a worship center for Ba'al (cf. Hosea 9:15, 12:11; see Hard Sayings of the Bible,
p. 330 and Roland deVaux, Ancient Israel, p. 303).

▣ "Beth-aven" This refers to Beth-el (cf. Hosea 4:15; 5:8; 10:5; Amos 5:5), "house of God," which
was sarcastically changed to "house of wickedness" (BDB 110). This was one of the two sites of the "golden calf"
worship set up by Jeroboam I (cf. 1 Kgs. 12:28-29). Originally the calf represented YHWH (cf. Exod. 32), but quickly
became corrupted into a fertility symbol.

▣ "And take the oath:

As the Lord lives'" This oath reflects the covenant name for
God, YHWH (cf. Exod. 3:14). The negative form Hosea 4:15c is implied in 15d-e.

SPECIAL TOPIC: CALL ON THE NAME

SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, D. (YHWH)

verses.zh: 以色列倔强，犹如倔强的母牛；现在耶和华要放他们，如同放羊羔在宽阔之地。
verses.en: Israel has rebelled[NOTE:1] like a stubborn heifer!Soon[NOTE:2] the Lord will put them out to pasturelike a lamb in a broad field.[NOTE:3]
notes: The Hebrew verb “has rebelled” (סָרַר, sarar) can also mean “to be stubborn.” This is the same root used in the simile: “like a stubborn (סֹרֵרָה, sorerah) heifer.” The similarity between Israel and a stubborn heifer is emphasized by the repetition of the same term.

The particle עַתָּה (ʿattah) often refers to the imminent or the impending future: “very soon” (BDB 774 s.v. עַתָּה 1.b). In Hosea it normally introduces imminent judgment (Hos 2:12; 4:16; 5:7; 8:8, 13; 10:2).

Or “How can the Lord feed them like a lamb in a meadow?” The syntax of this line is difficult and has been understood in two ways: (1) a declarative statement as an announcement of judgment (BDB 774 s.v. עַתָּה 1.b): “Now the Lord will feed them like a lamb in the broad field” (cf. KJV, ASV, NCV, NLT) or (2) as a rhetorical question lamenting the uncooperative spirit of Israel: “How can the Lord feed them like a lamb in a meadow?”; cf. NAB, NASB, NIV, NRSV, TEV), designed to produce a negative answer (“He cannot feed them…!”). However, this statement lacks an explicit interrogative marker. Although Hosea occasionally asks a rhetorical question without an explicit interrogative marker (e.g., 10:9; 13:14a), he normally does use a rhetorical particle to introduce rhetorical questions (e.g., 6:4; 8:5; 9:5, 14; 11:8; 13:9-10, 14b). Elsewhere, Hosea uses the introductory temporal adverb עַתָּה (“soon”) to introduce announcements of imminent future judgment (2:12; 4:16; 5:7; 8:8, 13; 10:2) and accusations of sin (5:3; 13:2). Although Israel has been as rebellious as a stubborn heifer, the Lord will indeed gain control of Israel: they will be like lambs (weakened and defeated) when he puts them out to pasture in a broad field (exile).
verses.commentary:
4:16 "Since Israel is stubborn,

Like a stubborn heifer" The term "stubborn" (BDB 710, KB 770) is
used twice comparing Israel with a non-cooperative (i.e. disobedient to authority) plow animal. This is often used of a
rebellious spirit:

- of a son, Deut. 21:18-21

- of a ruler, Isa. 1:23 (cf. Hosea 9:15)

- of children, Isa. 30:1

- of a people, Isa. 65:1-7

- of God's people, Jer. 6:28

"Stubborn" and "rebellious" often occur together (cf. Deut. 2:18,20; Ps. 78:8; Jer. 5:23).

SPECIAL TOPIC: STUBBORNNESS

▣ "Can the Lord now pasture them" This can be a statement or an
unmarked rhetorical question. Context implies a judgment scene (i.e. exile), not the tender care of a shepherd.

▣ "Like a lamb in a large field" Lambs do not like large fields, but small enclosures.

verses.zh: 以法莲亲近偶像，任凭他吧！
verses.en: Ephraim has attached himself to idols;Do not go near him!
verses.commentary:
4:17 "Ephraim is joined to idols" Ephraim was the largest tribe in the Northern Kingdom, so it stood for all the Northern Ten
Tribes. Their first king, Jeroboam I, was from the tribe of Ephraim. The term "joined" is a strong term for the political
(and by implication, religious) union between allies (BDB 287, KB 287, Qal PASSIVE PARTICIPLE, cf. Gen. 14:3).

David A. Hubbard, Hosea (The Tyndale OT Commentaries), suggests
that the term "joined" should be interpreted in light of its use in magical texts (cf. Deut. 18:11; Ps. 58:5). If so, Israel
has been "charmed" or "under a spell," possibly linked to 4:12; 5:4 (p. 110). My problem with this is not linguistic, but
theological. Personified evil should not be used as an excuse for fallen mankind's sin. These people sinned "open-eyed"
against the love of their covenant God. Though evil, both natural and personal, is a part of our fallen world, humans
are still responsible for their actions (cf. Hosea 4:18c).

SPECIAL TOPIC: PERSONAL EVIL

▣ "Let him alone" What a horrendous judgment (BDB 628, KB 679, Hiphil IMPERATIVE).
God allows His people to have their own desires and choices (and their consequences) because of their spiritual blindness
(cf. Hosea 5:4; Rom. 1:24, 26, 28).

verses.zh: 他们所喝的已经发酸，他们时常行淫，他们的官长最爱羞耻的事。
verses.en: They consume their alcohol, then engage in cult prostitution;they dearly love their shameful behavior.
verses.commentary:
4:18

NASB
"dearly love shame"

NKJV
"dearly love dishonor"

NRSV
"love lewdness more than their glory"

TEV
"preferring disgrace to honor"

REB
"devoted their lives to immorality"

NJB
"preferring Shame to Pride"

Peshitta
"love shame and idolatry"

LXX
"loved dishonor through her insolence"

NET
"dearly love their shameful behavior"

JPSOA
"they love beyond measure ‒ Disgrace is the 'gift'"

This is a good example of how checking different translations, ancient and modern, can demonstrate
the semantical field of a word or phrase. Often, it is the ambiguity of the MT or LXX that shows the problem.

The MT has "her shields" or "her princes" (i.e. "they loved dishonor and her shield"). The NRSV reflects
a possible option, according to the UBS Text Project, p. 234, but the UBS gives "her shields" or "her princes" a "B" rating.

- מגניה ‒ "her shield" (BDB 171, i.e. "rulers," NASB margin)

- מגאנם ‒ "more than their glory"

Happy hour is over! The term "rulers" is literally "shield" (BDB 171). It usually refers to political leaders, but
here it may include the priests and prophets (cf. Hosea 4:5).

verses.zh: 风把他们裹在翅膀里；他们因所献的祭必致蒙羞。
verses.en: A whirlwind has wrapped them in its wings;they will be brought to shame because of their idolatrous worship.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “their altars” (so NAB, NRSV) or “their sacrifices” (so KJV, NASB, NIV). Here זִבְחוֹתָם (zivkhotam, “altars; sacrifices”) is a metonymy of association for Israel’s apostate, idolatrous Baal worship.
verses.commentary:
4:19 "The wind wraps them in its wings" The "wings of the wind" are imagery for

- foreign alliances (cf. Hosea 12:1)

- YHWH's coming judgment (cf. Hosea 13:15, i.e. YHWH used Mesopotamian powers to exile His people, cf. Jer. 22:22)

- evil spiritual influences (i.e. "wind" translated "spirit," cf. Hosea 4:12; 5:4)

YHWH is depicted as riding on the wings of the wind (cf. 2 Sam. 22:11; Ps. 18:10; 104:3). YHWH's presence
can denote covenant safety (under the shadow of His wings) and protection or as here, covenant justice and the
consequences of covenant violations!

SPECIAL TOPIC: SHADOW AS A METAPHOR FOR PROTECTION AND CARE

▣

NASB, NKJV, NJB, REB, JPSOA
"their sacrifices"

TEV
"their pagan sacrifices"

LXX, Peshitta, NRSV
"their altars"

The UBS Text Project, pp. 234-235, gives "because of their sacrifices" a "C" rating
(i.e. highly doubtful). The only difference is vocalization.

- How does modern man participate in idolatry?

READING CYCLE THREE (see "Bible Interpretation Seminar")

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible.
Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing
is not inspired, but it is the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every paragraph has one and only one subject.

BASIC OUTLINE OF CHAPTERS 4-11

- Hosea 4-5 comprise a literary unit that describes Israel's faithlessness.

- Hosea 6-10 are a literary unit that describes Israel's punishment.

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: HOSEA 4:1-3

1Listen to the word of the Lord, O sons of Israel,

For the Lord has a case against the inhabitants of the land,

Because there is no faithfulness or kindness

Or knowledge of God in the land.

2There is swearing, deception, murder, stealing and adultery.

They employ violence, so that bloodshed follows bloodshed.

3Therefore the land mourns,

And everyone who lives in it languishes

Along with the beasts of the field and the birds of the sky,

And also the fish of the sea disappear.
